questions.q: Who does lesson 1 credit most for China's rise?
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the people had more influence than the government.

questions.q: What happened to production after the push for rapid industrialism?
a: Famine caused it to slide backward
questions.why: Lesson 1 says production grew at first but then slid back as famine hit.

questions.q: What does the 'barehanded' fortune idea describe?
a: Building wealth from nothing through one's own business
questions.why: Lesson 2 says ambition rose once individuals could start businesses.

questions.q: What did Gong Haiyan overcome, per lesson 2?
a: Being raised in a remote village by parents who couldn't read
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses her story as an example of ambition.

questions.q: What is the post-1980s generation nicknamed?
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the Chinese call them the 'Me' generation.
